checks.record: Recog 1.001`$P->P . P  .: P`=This is a perfectly correct application of MP.  The fact that the rule is stated using distinct antecedent and consequent allows the antecedent and consequent to be distinct, but does not require it.`&

checks.record: Recog 1.002`$~T->(T->U) . ~(T->U)  .: ~~T`=Note that the conclusion must be as given, and cannot be "T", which is not the negation of the antecedent of the conditional.`&

checks.record: Recog 1.004`$~(~P->W)  .: P->W`=The premise is the negation of a conditional, not the negation of a negation.  If the premise had been \l"~~(P->W)"\l the conclusion could have been obtained by DN.`&

checks.record: Recog 1.005`$~Q->~R . R  .: Q`=The second premise is not the negation of the consequent of the conditional (as is required), and the conclusion is not the negation of the antecedent of the conditional (as is also required).  The result can be obtained from those two premises, but not directly by a single application of MT.  Rather, one must first apply DN to the second premise, then apply MT to obtain \l"~~Q"\l, then apply a second DN to that result.`&
checks.activeRules: [R, DNE, DNI, MP, MT]
[R, DNE, DNI, MP, MT]

checks.record: Recog 1.009`$~~P->~Q . ~~Q  .: ~P`=This case is rather like 1.005.  Although MT can be applied directly to these premises, it yields \l"~~~P"\l rather than \l"~P"\l.  The latter requires an application of DN.`&

checks.record: Recog 1.010`$T->S  .: ~~(T->S)`=As in 1.007, the "official" outermost parentheses have been dropped in the premise, but cannot be dropped in the conclusion.`&

checks.record: Recog 1.011`$P->Y . ~P  .: ~Y`=A wrong way around attempt to apply MT.  To apply MT, the second premise must be the negation of the consequent of the conditional rather than being the negation of the antecedent.`&

checks.record: Recog 1.014`$~~~P->Q  .: ~P->Q`=If we restore the dropped parentheses, we will see that the premise is \l"(~~~P->Q)"\l, not \l"~~~(P->Q)"\l, and thus a conditional, not a negation. (Only when the derived rule of Interchange of Equivalents is established will any rules become applicable to the interior of formulas.)`&
checks.activeRules: [R, DNE, DNI, MP, MT]
